Documentation carries a lot of small status signals: which release a feature landed in, what is still experimental, what is deprecated and kept only for compatibility.
Written as prose they are easy to miss, and written as ad hoc HTML spans they drift apart the moment there is more than one page.

`badge` turns them into one configured vocabulary.
Each kind of badge is defined once, under `extensions.badge`, and then written as `{{{< badge key value >}}}` wherever the label belongs, including inside a heading.

## Installation

```bash
quarto add {{< var extension.reference >}}
```

This will install the extension under the `_extensions` subdirectory.
If you are using version control, you will want to check in this directory.

Or install it from your editor with [Quarto Wizard](https://m.canouil.dev/quarto-wizard):

::: {.btn-group role="group" aria-label="Quarto Wizard installer options"}

[Visual Studio Code](vscode://mcanouil.quarto-wizard/install?repo={{< var extension.wizard-reference >}}){.btn .btn-outline-primary title="Install {{< var extension.reference >}} in Visual Studio Code using the Quarto Wizard extension."}
[Positron](positron://mcanouil.quarto-wizard/install?repo={{< var extension.wizard-reference >}}){.btn .btn-outline-primary title="Install {{< var extension.reference >}} in Positron using the Quarto Wizard extension."}
[VSCodium](vscodium://mcanouil.quarto-wizard/install?repo={{< var extension.wizard-reference >}}){.btn .btn-outline-primary title="Install {{< var extension.reference >}} in VSCodium using the Quarto Wizard extension."}

:::

## Quick start

Define the badges once, in `_quarto.yml` for a whole project or in a document's front matter for a single page:

```yaml
extensions:
  badge:
    - key: stable
      colour: springgreen
    - key: experimental
      class: bg-info
```

Then write the shortcode wherever the label belongs:

```markdown
Version {{{< badge stable 2.5.0 >}}}, beside a feature still marked {{{< badge experimental alpha >}}}.
```

Which renders as: Version {{< badge stable 2.5.0 >}}, beside a feature still marked {{< badge experimental alpha >}}.

The first argument is the key, which selects the configuration, and the second is the value shown inside the badge.

See the [Reference](reference.qmd) for every option, and the [Examples](examples.qmd) for each of them rendered.

## Where it works

HTML output formats only.
The shortcode contributes raw HTML, so in every other format the badge is dropped and the surrounding text is left intact.

Every user-supplied value is HTML-escaped before it is written to the document.
